en.title: Netflix's Best Musicals: Why 'Emilia Pérez' Missed the Cut
en.summary: Netflix has become a surprising haven for original musicals, but one highly anticipated film has landed on the wrong side of critical reception. We dive into why 'Emilia Pérez' failed to make a top 10 list, despite its award buzz.
en.body:
Netflix has cultivated a vibrant space for original musical films, offering everything from Broadway-style spectacles to unique genre blends. Yet, not every musical gem shines equally bright on the platform. While **Emilia Pérez** has garnered significant attention and awards, including a Best Supporting Actress win for **Zoe Saldaña**, it notably failed to secure a spot on What's on Netflix's recent list of the 10 best original musical features. The omission stems from a strong critical stance against its narrative choices and representation.

The source material pulls no punches, labeling **Emilia Pérez** as "bad" and "possibly one of the worst musicals of the decade," even calling its awards run a "psy-op." This harsh critique is rooted in concerns over its portrayal of Mexican stereotypes and, more significantly, its handling of transgender representation. Critics like those at NPR have pointed out the film's potential for stereotyping, suggesting it falls short in its depiction of trans women. While the film's director, **Jacques Audiard**, is known for his distinctive cinematic style, and its unusual musical approach garnered praise at Cannes, its reception in the United States, particularly on a platform like Netflix, has been divisive.

## The Divisive Nature of 'Emilia Pérez'

The exclusion of **Emilia Pérez** from "best of" lists highlights a crucial conversation among fans and critics about representation in film. For a platform that reaches a global audience, the way sensitive topics like gender identity and cultural stereotypes are handled is paramount. While **Emilia Pérez** boasts a star-studded cast including **Selena Gomez** and **Zoe Saldaña**, and received accolades such as the César Award for Best Film, its narrative missteps appear to have overshadowed its technical merits for some viewers and critics. The film's R rating, citing sexual material, language, and violent content, further indicates its mature and potentially challenging themes.

## What Fans Are Saying

Online discussions surrounding **Emilia Pérez** reveal a split audience. Some viewers praised its boldness and unique blend of crime drama and musical, while others echoed the critical concerns about its stereotyping. The debate underscores the growing demand for authentic and nuanced storytelling, especially within the LGBTQ+ community. For fans of musicals, the disappointment lies not just in a film's potential quality but in its responsibility to represent diverse experiences with respect and depth. The fact that **The Prom**, another Netflix musical, was also noted for its potential drawbacks (specifically, **James Corden**'s significant screen time), suggests that Netflix's musical output, while plentiful, faces high expectations regarding both entertainment value and sensitive portrayal.

## What's Next

While **Emilia Pérez** might not be topping the charts for musical excellence on Netflix, the platform continues to invest in the genre. Future original musical projects are expected, and the ongoing success of films like **The Unauthorized Bash Brothers Experience** – a beloved, albeit short, visual album by **The Lonely Island** – shows the diverse range of musical content Netflix is willing to embrace. Fans will be watching closely to see how the platform navigates creative ambition with responsible storytelling in its upcoming musical endeavors.

Its entire awards run was a psy‑op. The ones on this list are better, further, faster, stronger, and decidedly less problematic. ( The Prom might’ve made the cut if it weren’t for James Corden’s major screen time.) 10 The Lonely Island Presents: The Unauthorized Bash Brothers Experience It is a crime that The Lonely Island’s silly visual album starring Andy Samberg and Akiva Schaffer as the titular baseball stars Jose Canseco and Mark McGwire is only 30 minutes long. I needed ten more minutes. No, an hour. Nevertheless, it’s one of the best musical projects on the platform. I’m calling it a movie. You can’t stop me. The Unauthorized Bash Brothers Experience is a hysterical, psychedelic laugh riot that serves as a fun follow‑up to their masterpiece Popstar: Never Stop Never Stopping , packed with unforgettable tunes. I still crack up over Andy screaming “JOSE” and Schaffer’s nonchalant, “and I’m Mark.” Nothing will hit the serotonin highs of seeing Stephanie Beatriz, HAIM, and Maya Rudolph crossover to sing about IHOP and forcing the boys to shake their butts. Peak cinema. 9 LEO Adam Sandler as a walking, talking, 50-something 5th-grade class lizard who becomes a moral compass to his students is such a charming little movie about growing up. Well, if you can move past the gross-out jokes and bizarre product placements. Yet, it has a positive cynicism that more films should strive for. Much of that is thanks to Robert Smigel and Sandler’s joint script and the silly tunes provided. Granted, none of them are particularly memorable, but the story and Sandler’s deep, crotchety voice coming out of this kind‑hearted lizard are so delightful that it barely matters. 8 My Little Pony: A New Generation Man—or, mane—it’s bizarre that a My Little Pony reboot pushed itself to tell a story about unity with themes of misinformation and bigotry, and somehow pulled it off staggeringly well.
